prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit this pixel-art bone-heap concept. The requested change is SMALLER INDIVIDUAL BONES, NOT A SMALLER WHOLE HEAP.
Replace every large long bone, oversized curved bone and broad flat plate with several much shorter smaller differently shaped broken fragments. Individual pieces should be about HALF their current length and bulk. Keep the overall heap footprint approximately the same, low and compact. About 12-16 visible small pieces, some overlapping and partially buried: tiny short shafts, thin splinters, short curved fragments, small flat chips and small knobbly ends. These must still look like dry bone, not pebbles.
No single bone should span more than one quarter of the heap's width. No dominant long bone or large loop. Bone shapes should differ within this ONE heap. All together in one compact low mound, no separate clusters, ring or anatomically arranged skeleton.
Preserve the simple chunky pixel art, muted ivory/taupe/purple-gray palette, three-quarter overhead camera, top-left light and sparse shading of the input. Crisp square pixel clusters, hard stepped edges, no smoothing, gradients, glow or alpha halo. No skull, face, jaw, ribs, large plate, flesh, blood, floor, rocks, tiles, text or background.
Truly transparent background. Keep rendering simple: finer bones, not more surface detail.
